newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Brierley raises 20 billion yen.
newsitem.headline: Brierley raises 20 billion yen.

text.p: Brierley Investments Ltd on Wednesday confirmed it had raised 20 billion yen through a 10-year private placement by Japanese insurance companies.
The issue was priced at 100 basis points over the 10-year Japanese government bond rate.
Chief Financial Officer Herman Rockefeller said the issue was initially for 10 billion yen but it was increased because of demand.
He said the rate was very attractive and given that the average duration of BIL's assets was 7-8 years the maturity was ideal.

"It gives us a diversified funding source in the sense of moving away from just the banking market and of course being in the Japanese market as well," he said. "The fact that they are willing to back us for such a high amount is certainly a strong vote of confidence."
He said it was really a rearrangement and bank funding would be repaid as it matured. The yen exposure would be hedged.
HSBC Markets in association with HongKongBank New Zealand arranged the issue on behalf of BIL Asia Group Treasury, Hong Kong branch.
The issue is guaranteed by BIL and BIL (Australia Finance).

The money would be used to pay back debts at roll-over dates. It changed the profile of the company's debt from bank to non-bank loans, increased the level of fixed-rate debt and the maturity of the debt.
The issue follows one in May when BIL raised NZ$333 million through a three-year transferable loan facility.
Rockefeller said BIL would soon have a large amount of cash on deposit as the new arrangement would be signed in Hong Kong on October 8 and be drawn down the following day.
Proceeds from BIL's selldown of its British hotels group Thistle would arrive the next day.
